stem: In a survey of 600 adults in Chattogram, \(45\%\) said they own a bicycle. Of the adults who own a bicycle, \(30\%\) said they ride it to work. How many of the 600 adults said they ride a bicycle to work?
solution: Owners who ride to work: \(0.30 \cdot 270 = 81\) adults.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the percents, \(45\% + 30\% = 75\%\), and taking \(75\%\) of 600.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(30\%\) of all 600 adults. The \(30\%\) applies only to the 270 adults who own a bicycle.
explanation.C: Correct. \(30\%\) of the 270 bicycle owners is \(0.30 \cdot 270 = 81\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the number of adults who own a bicycle. One more step is needed.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'D': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'A': 'C', 'C': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'D', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'A', 'D': 'C'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
owners = Rational(45, 100) * 600
assert owners == 270
v = Rational(30, 100) * owners
assert v == 81
assert value(choices[answer]) == v
assert all(value(choices[k]) != v for k in choices if k != answer)
